skill.name: hugging-face-cli
skill.description: Guides safe use of the Hugging Face Hub CLI for models, datasets, Spaces, jobs, repositories, cache, and authentication workflows.
skill.summary: Use the Hugging Face Hub CLI to manage Hub resources from AI coding tools.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are Markdown command references, not executable Ruby backticks. Real risks remain around remote installer snippets, token and secret handling, destructive Hub operations, extension execution, and community provenance claims.

remediation.issue: Remote installer snippets download scripts and execute them with shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer package manager installation. If shell installers remain, require checksum verification, script review, and explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: Community source metadata claims official upstream provenance.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that this marketplace package is community sourced, or separate upstream attribution from trust and review status.

remediation.issue: Commands can expose tokens, modify secrets, and pass secrets into jobs or Spaces.
remediation.suggestion: Add guardrails that prevent token printing and require confirmation before any secret, token, environment, or credential action.

remediation.issue: Commands can delete or change remote Hugging Face resources.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for deletes, uploads, syncs with delete flags, endpoint changes, webhooks, volumes, and repository settings.

remediation.issue: Extension commands can install and execute third-party code.
remediation.suggestion: Require source review and user confirmation before installing, updating, or executing hf extensions from public repositories.

content.user_title: Manage Hugging Face Hub from the CLI
content.value_statement: Managing Hub resources across models, datasets, Spaces, and jobs can require many commands. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured hf CLI guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains common hf CLI commands for models, datasets, Spaces, repos, papers, jobs, and webhooks.
Guides authentication workflows with hf auth commands and HF_TOKEN usage.
Documents cache inspection, pruning, removal, and verification commands.
Covers Hub uploads, downloads, repository settings, branches, tags, and pull requests.
Describes hf-mount setup and mount commands for Hub repositories and buckets.
limitations: It does not install the hf CLI automatically.
It cannot verify current Hugging Face pricing, quotas, or API behavior without external checks.
Several commands can change, delete, or publish remote Hub resources.
Token, secret, and extension commands require explicit user approval.

use_cases.title: Download and Inspect Model Assets
use_cases.description: Find the right hf download, model info, and cache commands for local model workflows.

use_cases.title: Operate Hub Repositories and Jobs
use_cases.description: Plan repository, endpoint, job, webhook, and Space changes with clear command references.

use_cases.title: Explore Datasets and Papers
use_cases.description: Use dataset, paper, collection, and leaderboard commands to inspect Hub resources.

prompt_templates.title: Show Basic Hub Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner check before using the CLI.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show me which hf commands can check the installed CLI, active account, and basic help output. Do not reveal tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Model Download
prompt_templates.scenario: Download a model with filters and cache awareness.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an hf download for a Hugging Face model. Include options for revision, include patterns, local directory, and dry run behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Upload
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a Hub upload before it changes a repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hf CLI reference to prepare an upload plan for a model repo. Include privacy, branch, include, exclude, and pull request options.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Operations Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced Hub operations with approval points.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an hf CLI workflow for jobs, endpoints, and webhooks. Mark every command that needs confirmation because it changes resources or uses secrets.

output_examples.input: I need to download one model revision into a local folder.
output_examples.output: A short command plan naming the download command, revision option, local directory option, and dry run check before transfer.

output_examples.input: I need to update a Space secret and restart the Space.
output_examples.output: A step plan that separates secret update, restart, and verification, with explicit approval before changing the Space.

output_examples.input: I need to clean local Hugging Face cache safely.
output_examples.output: A cache maintenance plan that lists inspection, dry run, pruning, and checksum verification steps before removal.

best_practices: Use dry run, preview, or list commands before uploads, deletions, syncs, and cache removals.
Prefer HF_TOKEN environment variables over passing tokens directly in command arguments.
Verify installer scripts, extension sources, and destructive operations with the user before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not print authentication tokens into chat, logs, or shared terminal output.
Do not run curl-to-shell installers without reviewing the downloaded script and source.
Do not delete repositories, buckets, endpoints, webhooks, or volumes without explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill install the Hugging Face CLI?
faq.answer: No. It describes installation commands and asks for review before local execution.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it manage private Hugging Face resources?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user provides valid authentication and approves each sensitive action.

faq.question: Does it expose tokens by default?
faq.answer: No. Some documented commands can print or use tokens, so outputs must be handled carefully.

faq.question: Can it run remote jobs or endpoints?
faq.answer: It documents hf commands for jobs and endpoints, but execution depends on user credentials and approval.

faq.question: Is the command list always current?
faq.answer: No. Verify command behavior against current Hugging Face documentation before production changes.
